rendered: The largest printed estimate in Table 1[1] is for Section 9 – Ultra-High-Speed (Thick)[2] Electrode Processing[3], at 325-350^b[4] Wh/kg. However, its footnote says: Through combination of method approaches discussed in Sections 5-7.[5] That value is therefore a combined estimate rather than an individual implementation, which the table caption describes: Estimations of electrode property and cell energy density improvements from individual implementation of the technologies discussed in Sections 4-10.[6] Among individually implemented technologies, the largest estimate is for Section 6 – Low-Co/Ni-Rich Cathodes (i.e.[7] NMC 811)[8], at 275–300[9] Wh/kg.
